title: Philippines, Australia reaffirm defense ties
summary: The Philippines and Australia yesterday reaffirmed their defense ties as they expressed “concern over what they described as “coercive, aggressive and dangerous” against Filipino…

blocks.text: Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese (L) walks out with Philippines' President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. after his address to the House of Representatives at the Parliament House in Canberra on February 29, 2024. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos told Australia's parliament on February 29 that his country was on the "frontline" of a battle against powers undermining regional peace, but would not capitulate in maritime disputes with the likes of China.

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines and Australia yesterday reaffirmed their defense ties as they expressed “concern over what they described as “coercive, aggressive and dangerous” against Filipino ships in the South China Sea.

In a joint statement released after a bilateral meeting between President Marcos and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, the two countries vowed to deepen their political and strategic cooperation and strengthen engagement between their officials and armed forces.

“The Philippines and Australia reaffirm our Strategic Partnership, established in 2023 and underpinned by longstanding cooperation, shared democratic values and a common vision for a peaceful, stable and prosperous region where strategic agency is freely exercised and sovereignty is upheld,” the statement read.

“As we commemorate the 80th year of the establishment of our diplomatic relations this year, and at a time of rising uncertainties, we commit to expand our bilateral security and defense relations,” it added. The two countries also reiterated the importance of peace and stability in the maritime domain.

“We remain seriously concerned about the situation in the South China Sea, particularly the coercive, aggressive, and dangerous actions against Filipino nationals and vessels. In the tenth anniversary year of the South China Sea Arbitral Tribunal Award of 12 July 2016, we reaffirm the final and binding nature of the Award on the parties to the Arbitration,” they said.

The Philippines and Australia also committed to “expand cooperation and act in support of maritime safety and security, freedom of navigation and overflight and other lawful uses of the seas in accordance with the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.”
Also during the ASEAN-Australia Summit, Albanese announced a new digital cooperation package designed to deepen Australia’s partnership with the regional bloc.

“It will accelerate ASEAN’s digital transformation and boost economic growth by strengthening the region’s digital ecosystem, supporting AI safety standards and building a digital workforce,” Albanese said.
